<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with clean framing, but CON won the decisive clash over what Iran's distance to a bomb is actually made of. PRO built a strong case (irreversible industrial destruction, closing window, correctly-assessed and empirically bounded retaliation, proliferation cascade), and deserves credit for epistemic discipline in refusing to invent a magnitude figure. However, PRO's two load-bearing planks were each squarely damaged. First, PRO's sharpest attack — that CON contradicted itself by saying a warehouse cascade suffices while also saying inspectors kept the program honest [A4.5] — was directly and elegantly resolved in [B4.3]-[B4.4]: cameras guarded the feedstock, a warehouse cascade is useless without it, and the strikes effectively diverted the HEU off the books without Tehran ever breaking a seal. That converted PRO's best offense into CON's best offense. Second, PRO's "restraint produced 60%" narrative was historically undercut in [B2.1] (60% began after U.S. withdrawal from a deal with cameras on cascade halls) and PRO never squarely answered it, retreating to "eroded transparency." PRO's "standing veto" also never survived CON's pressure question: PRO's reply rested on Iranian "belief" and generic intelligence capacity, which CON punished with the Fordow-was-hidden-for-years point, and PRO left CON's "follow-on strikes make wider-war risk recurring rather than bounded" argument largely unanswered — which matters directly to the "despite the risk" clause in the motion. PRO's closing "security as a cancellable subscription" reframe was the best rhetorical moment of the debate, but CON's closing answered it head-on: cancellation was the alarm, and the strikes cancelled the subscription while keeping none of the alarm. CON's two clipped turns are a real execution cost, and CON's answer on what Iran had actually agreed to concede was partly assertion, which keeps this competitive rather than lopsided.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B4.3]-[B4.4]: answering PRO's contradiction charge by showing the cameras guarded the feedstock (not merely buildings), so "notification is the barrier," and the strikes accomplished Iran's diversion for it — turning PRO's strongest attack into CON's central indictment.</best_rebuttal>
